data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The Collatz conjecture is unsettled and false; there exists a divergent trajectory that escapes to infinity via a pseudo-random growth phase that never hits a power of 2.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Proof that the density of such 'escaping' integers is zero","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Proof that any sequence eventually encounters a sufficiently large power of 2 to crash it back down","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The existence of a starting value n such that the ratio of '3n+1' steps to 'n/2' steps asymptotically exceeds log(2)/log(3), preventing the sequence from ever returning to a lower value.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
